主要内容: The second year of U.K. gender pay gap reporting has revealed little progress, with over 10,000 companies submitting their data. Some major firms reported that the pay gap between men and women has widened. The requirement for companies with at least 250 employees to report gender pay gaps has led to the release of embarrassing data, highlighting the underrepresentation of women in higher-paying roles. Despite these findings, companies emphasize that meaningful change takes time and that conclusions from just two years of data are limited. The pay gap data is presented on a mean and median hourly basis, with some companies showing a pay gap greater than 70 percent. The report does not adjust for factors such as experience or location, providing a blunt assessment across the entire workforce.
